conflicts.fact: What the Lesson 1 predict-phase question/prediction was about (the anchoring phenomenon wording)
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1: prediction prompt is 'Why can a mosquito drink blood but a grasshopper cannot?' / why different animals have different feeding structures. Lesson 3: says Lesson 1 prediction cards answered 'Why does a mosquito leave only a tiny dot on your skin while a grasshopper leaves ragged holes in a maize leaf?'

conflicts.fact: Which lesson the cumulative model/table was started in and what it is
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1: a single-animal annotated sketch model of ONE chosen animal. Lesson 2: Lesson 1 drew a sketch of all five organisms with question marks. Lesson 3: 'cumulative mouthpart diversity model' started in Lesson 1. Lesson 4: 'feeding-structures comparison table' started in Lesson 2 and extended in Lesson 3, and described as having four columns but listing five.

conflicts.fact: Lion dental formula total vs. Lion dentition and tooth counts / animal observed in video
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6: lion I 3/3, C 1/1, PM 3/2, M 1/1 ×2 = 30 (real lion formula 3/3,1/1,3/2,1/1 =30, fine), but clip described as 'a wildebeest chewing cud' in observe phase vs 'cow chewing cud' in Observed summary; Lesson 6 also says cow's 'dental pad' / 'lack upper incisors' consistent. Minor inconsistency in what animal chews cud.

conflicts.fact: Where the question about what happens inside the grasshopper after chewing is answered / Lesson numbering
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2: says internal digestion question 'lives in Lessons 7 and 8'. Lesson 7 and 8 cover human digestion, not grasshopper; Lesson 8 DQB claims Lesson 1 asked how a grasshopper digests maize leaves, which Lesson 1 did not ask about as such.

conflicts.fact: Anchoring phenomenon mosquito digestion claim: mosquito bypasses digestion vs. mosquito delivers amino acids to gut for absorption
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7: mosquito draws blood directly into gut, bypasses all digestion steps / needs no complex digestive system. Lesson 9: blood delivers ready-made amino acids directly, bypassing mechanical digestion only (implying chemical digestion/absorption still occur).

Lesson 3: saliva prevents clotting (or aids sap flow). Lesson 8: mosquito uses salivary enzymes to prevent clotting, compared to amylase digesting food, implying digestive function; Lesson 3 treats it as anticoagulant, not digestion.

conflicts.fact: Where amylase acts and starch digestion location
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7: amylase in mouth and pancreatic juice in small intestine. Lesson 8: amylase in saliva and small intestine, and asks where else amylase acts, 'why produced in two places'; also Lesson 8 says pepsin breaks down proteins in nyama choma and lipase breaks fat from avocado, while Lesson 7 uses sukuma wiki/cooking fat as substrates.

conflicts.fact: Length of the small intestine model and total model length
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7: small intestine rope 6–7 m, total model ~9 m, and stocking for large intestine; overview lists 'stocking' for large intestine while kit also lists rectum container and 'rope' for small intestine, whereas overview says 'balloons...funnel...stocking to represent oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine' (stocking/tubing assigned differently).

conflicts.fact: Lesson 4 title/framing vs content for flamingo
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 title asks 'How does a fish eagle eat what a flamingo cannot?' but lesson never covers flamingo; Lesson 1 lists flamingo/fish eagle as in the Lake Nakuru scene; Lesson 5 covers flamingo. Also Lesson 4 overview contrasts fish eagle with a hornbill, while predict phase says hornbill beak at Arabuko-Sokoke.
